findings.suggested_fix: Seed today's appointments with mixed statuses (Scheduled, Completed, No-show, Cancelled) and require the dashboard counts to equal the day schedule counts for that mix.
findings.text: S-2 AC1 seeds only Scheduled appointments, so a dashboard that counts only Scheduled (a rejected A-02 option) passes even if the day schedule also counts Completed or No-show. The AC does not catch the likeliest wrong implementation of REQ-4.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-2 AC: at 11:00 local with unbooked slots at 11:00 and 11:30, the next free slot shows 11:30 and the 11:00 slot is not counted as free (or state the rule the day schedule applies).
findings.text: REQ-6 says the next free slot 'starts after now', but no AC covers a slot that starts exactly now. That is the limit boundary where an off-by-one (>= vs >) bug in the next-free and free-count logic would show.

findings.text: S-6 AC3 and AC4 Then clauses say 'look and behave exactly as before the change' without naming an observable (tile counts, link targets, list rows), so they are weak to check.

rubric_items.reason: All 14 known REQs (REQ-1..REQ-14) are traced by at least one story; no assumed REQs exist.
S-1..S-5 each carry one outcome; S-6 bundles three separate outcomes (Period independence, no contact details, rest unchanged).
Time-zone and inactive ACs discriminate well, but S-2 AC1 would pass a Scheduled-only count, the slot-starting-exactly-now boundary of REQ-6 is missing, and S-6 AC3/AC4 lean on 'exactly as before'.
Values come from the intent (Asia/Kolkata, next 10, labels); the 19:00 UTC instant is derived inline from UTC+05:30; times like 11:00 are test fixtures.
Consistent terms (On duty today, day schedule, Fully booked), uniform Given/When/Then, readable fixtures.
